sentences.text: Khaan is an extinct oviraptorid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia.
Physically, this animal resembled other members of its group.
Evidence suggests the creature was likely covered in feathers.
The main specimens discovered together measured about four feet in length.
However, a third individual, cataloged as IGM 100/973, was found to be considerably larger than the primary group.
The species Khaan mckennai was formally named by James M. Clark and colleagues in the year 2001.
The specific name mckennai was chosen to honor the paleontologist Malcolm Carnegie McKenna.
Dietary habits likely included small vertebrates such as mammals, lizards, and possibly other small dinosaurs.
A 2022 study indicates that Khaan possessed a very strong bite force compared to other oviraptorosaurs.
Although a moderate jaw gape often signals herbivory, this animal probably fed on tougher vegetation than other herbivorous theropods like ornithomimosaurs and therizinosaurs.
Khaan is classified within the family Oviraptoridae.
Among oviraptorids, this dinosaur was likely more closely related to Conchoraptor.
The estimated time range for the species spans from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
The diet of oviraptorids like Khaan is debated, with suggestions ranging from plants to molluscs.
Examinations suggest oviraptorosaurs may have been either powerful-biting generalists or specialists utilizing niche partitioning based on body size and cranial function.
